heard: A massive canyon system on Mars stretches nearly 4,000 kilometers long. The historic Mariner 9 orbiter first revealed this colossal scar across the planet in 1971. Its staggering length matches the entire distance from New York City all the way to Lowe's Angels. This solar system, record breaker plunges down to 11 kilometers deep in certain vast regions. Ancient volcanic activity from the Tharsis bulge stressed the planetary crust until it split wide open. Colossal gravitational landslides then widened the gorge, sending debris rushing over 100 kilometers across the floor. Hydrated minerals preserved inside prove ancient water once helped shape this record breaker. These cataclysms explain why.
